sourceInformation.source: Demon Attack (Imagic, 1982), chiefly the Atari 2600 version by Rob Fulop
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 (R180), WebGPURenderer with WebGL 2 fallback; Rapier 2D 0.19.3 WASM; Web Audio; Gamepad API; WebRTC; AI Hub Session Protocol v1, client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded polygonal demons, bold ink contours, ice-moon diorama and printed arcade typography
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and keyframe tracks for wings, breathing, crowns, seals and cannon recoil; procedural movement and particles
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-written chiptune music (10% default), oscillator/noise effects and formant-synthesized gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–4-player authoritative shared-world AI Hub co-op; 2-player standalone WebRTC with manual invitation/reply codes; 2-player couch co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless scripts, deterministic full campaign simulation, synthetic controller, touch emulation, generated-audio analysis, two-page network tests and official AI Hub harness; screenshots for visual composition; WebKit compatibility and direct file URL verified. Physical controller feel, real iOS behavior, audible mix quality and arbitrary cross-internet peer connectivity: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Original Imagic manual; archived screenshots and gameplay footage at Atarimania; sound-effect source-code reference; official Three.js, Rapier and AI Hub documentation
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux, Ubuntu 26.04.1 on WSL2

testingFeedback: 4 implementation issues were caught by automated tests; multiplayer flow review found 2 more. All were fixed. Headless timing and screenshot failures were addressed in the test harness separately.

3 automated-test issues were game breaking: a wave-transition physics exception, a startup syntax error, and multi-view renderer initialization failure. Review also found a critical peer-to-solo state reset issue.
The deterministic full-campaign bot playthrough: all six waves, split/diving demons, beam attacks, pulse returns, pickups, both upgrade stops, boss phases, victory and endless encore.
Initial software-WebGPU screenshots were blank. They were replaced by state/draw-call checks and WebGL captures for visual inspection.
engineFeedback: Three’s native animation clips and toon materials work well together for an entirely procedural cast.
A Rapier WASM stack overflow appeared at a wave transition; creating a fresh world per wave resolved it. Multiple software GPU views also needed initialization recovery to WebGL.
The fixed-step arcade simulation, controller-focused screens, and authoritative cooperative networking.
Coordinating physics lifetimes and renderer startup with the Hub session lifecycle across several browser views.
An integrated toon-outline effect with consistent WebGPU and WebGL behavior.
promptFeedback: The source-first brief, complete-demo scope and controller-first requirement made the design direction clear.
The scope of standalone online play versus Hub sessions required a choice; both were implemented.
Combining a single-file package, modern GPU rendering, complete progression and several input/network paths.
Specify the target standalone online signaling service, and distinguish required from optional cross-browser fallbacks.

aiHub.name: Demon Bonanza
aiHub.tagline: Cold moon. Hot cannon. Bad company.
aiHub.description: An ice-moon arcade shooter full of winged trouble: slide, steer tracer fire and reflect the barrage. Survive six waves, dethrone a three-phase demon monarch, and share your bunker stock with friends.
aiHub.controls: A/D or left stick: slide; mouse or right stick: aim; Space/LMB or R2: fire; E/RMB or Square: pulse; Shift or Circle: dash; Esc or Options: pause. Touch: drag, assisted auto-fire; two fingers: pulse.
